decidable_rule: the handle must resolve to a named dataset with an open licence text and a per-row table/figure locator before any row may be exported; failing that the verdict is not_verifiable and the ceiling is Tier C

identifiability.reason: no DOI, repository record, licence text, named dataset or table/figure index can be tied to the handle from inside this repository, and the probe makes no network request; a licence verdict therefore cannot be read and the source may not be imported

physics_reason.consequence: such a set can only ever enter as Tier C (feature, descriptor or ranking signal), never as a label for the liquid-phase experimental target, because the quantity computed is not the quantity predicted
physics_reason.kirkwood_relation: (eps - 1)(2 eps + 1) / (9 eps) = (4 pi N / 3) (alpha + mu^2 g / (3 k T))
physics_reason.statement: a gas-phase computed epsilon and a liquid-phase experimental epsilon are different quantities
physics_reason.why_g_is_one_in_gas: a single-molecule DFPT calculation has no orientational correlation, so g = 1 by construction; the computed number is a molecular polarisability, not the bulk liquid permittivity

row_level_classification.note: no row is classified: the source cannot be identified well enough to read a licence or locate a row, so no count is invented

tier_rule: a gas-phase computed epsilon is a different quantity from a liquid-phase experimental epsilon (missing orientational correlation g), so the set may only ever enter as Tier C
